newsitem.title: USA: Argument date set for Columbus tax case appeal.
newsitem.headline: Argument date set for Columbus tax case appeal.

text.p: Oral arguments before the U.S. Court of Appeals have been scheduled Feb. 24 for Columbus, Ohio's appeal of U.S. Tax Court ruling denying tax exemption for a city bond issue, according to David Rogers, a partner at the law firm of Bricker & Eckler, which represents the city.

Columbus filed the appeal after a tax court judge in July refused to reconsider his May 14 ruling in favor of the Internal Revenue Service's contention that bonds Columbus wants to issue to refund taxable notes it sold to pay off a pension liability would be arbitrage bonds and not eligible for tax exemption.
While awaiting an ultimate decision on the tax status of general obligation bonds it hopes to sell, Columbus privately placed $27 million of taxable bond anticipation notes with a money market fund.
Proceeds from the note issue, which matures on Jan. 30, 1997, were used to prepay a discounted liability Columbus owned the Ohio Police and Firemen's Disability and Pension Fund.
